ai-at-work.title: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
ai-at-work.excerpt: Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, even as delays at a Microsoft data center raise questions about its financing model.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nebius is betting $40 billion on AI infrastructure by essentially asking customers to pay upfront while banking on future revenue to cover the loans. This matters because digital workplace leaders are increasingly dependent on these emerging cloud providers for AI tools and services, so understanding their financial stability directly impacts your tech roadmap decisions. Honestly, funding massive infrastructure buildouts through customer prepayments feels like asking your employees to finance the office renovation before you've actually built the building, which should make any procurement team nervous.

ai-at-work.title: Jensen Huang was having a third affair, Reuters reports
ai-at-work.excerpt: Reuters is withholding the name of the new employee linked to Huang, but says she is an employee of Nvidia.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Reuters reported that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was involved in a third affair with a current Nvidia employee, though they've kept her identity private. This matters because leadership scandals involving power imbalances with direct reports create real governance headaches for any organization, not least one as influential as Nvidia. Look, we've all seen the "ethics training" slides, but nothing quite drives home the importance of actual accountability structures like watching a billionaire CEO get caught doing exactly what the handbook says not to do.

ai-at-work.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
ai-at-work.excerpt: Jensen Huang’s resignation raises questions about Nvidia’s commitment to open source AI, including its Hugging Face acquisition, open-weight models, and advocacy against restrictions, as the company n
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Jensen Huang stepping down from day-to-day operations at Nvidia has people wondering if the company will keep backing open source AI projects and the Hugging Face acquisition it made. For digital workplace folks, this matters because open source tools and models are increasingly central to how organizations build AI infrastructure and collaborate internally. My take: Nvidia's open source play always felt like a calculated hedge anyway, so don't expect dramatic reversals, but watch if the new leadership gets quieter about it.

ai-at-work.title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks
ai-at-work.excerpt: The airline said it will not allow customers to use AI agents to book flights and manage reservations.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: United Airlines is blocking AI agents from booking flights on their platform, saying it's a cybersecurity risk. This matters because it signals that even cutting-edge companies are hitting the brakes on AI automation when account access and payment systems are involved, which should make any digital workplace leader think twice about blindly deploying agents across sensitive processes. After 30 years in this space, I'd say United just did what most of us should be doing anyway: asking "should we?" before asking "can we?"

tools-tech.title: If the November Windows update fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do
tools-tech.excerpt: This month’s security update is failing on some systems already running the preview update released in October. But there is a fix afoot.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft's November Windows update is bricking installations on machines that already have the October preview version installed, though a workaround exists. Digital workplace teams need to know this because a failed critical security update can lock down entire fleets of devices and create support nightmares across the organization. After three decades watching these cycles, I'll say it plainly: preview versions exist for a reason, and pushing them into production environments before the final release ships is how you end up explaining to executives why half the company can't log in on a Tuesday morning.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft struggles to get M365 services back online after widespread outage
tools-tech.excerpt: If you’re struggling to send or receive emails, you’re not alone. Microsoft has been unable to fully restore Microsoft 365 more than 13 hours after an Exchange Online failure took down Outlook and spr
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft's Exchange Online went down hard on November 12th and stayed down for over 13 hours, cascading failures across Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Copilot while their fixes repeatedly flopped. This matters because half the working world relies on M365 for basic communication and collaboration, so when it breaks this badly your entire digital workplace strategy becomes theoretical. After 30 years in this space, I can tell you that depending on any single vendor for your critical infrastructure while their troubleshooting keeps failing is exactly the kind of risk conversation that should've happened years ago in your architecture planning.

tools-tech.title: United Airlines becomes the latest enterprise to shut its door to customer bots
tools-tech.excerpt: United Airlines on Wednesday became the latest enterprise to block customer bots, following similar moves from Walmart, Target and Amazon. The $59 billion airline, the second largest in the world, sai
tools-tech.dwp_take: United Airlines joined Walmart, Target, and Amazon in blocking customer bots, citing concerns about data leaks, accidental purchases, and regulatory violations. This matters to digital workplace pros because it signals that enterprises are finally waking up to the real risks of uncontrolled automation in customer-facing systems. Here's the thing: we spent years hyping bots as the future, and now the adults are taking the wheel back because somebody had to actually think about what happens when your bot books a $5,000 flight for nobody.

tools-tech.title: AI-related job creation to outpace losses by 2030, says Gartner
tools-tech.excerpt: Wider use of AI within organizations will lead to more jobs being created than are lost by 2030, according to Gartner. Around 10.6 million jobs will be added globally (excluding China and India) by th
tools-tech.dwp_take: Gartner's predicting that AI will create 1.7 million more jobs than it destroys globally by 2030, with 10.6 million new roles offset by 8.9 million losses. This matters because digital workplace teams need to start planning skills development and role transitions now instead of waiting for disruption to hit. The real question isn't whether the net numbers work out, it's whether your organization will be smart enough to upskill people for those new jobs or whether you'll just become another "sorry, your role doesn't exist anymore" statistic.

digital-culture.title: Kalshi will pay you $120,000 to play ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
digital-culture.excerpt: People are already calling out sick to play the feverishly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI. Companies like Logitech are even giving staff paid time off to partake. Now, thanks to prediction market Kal
digital-culture.dwp_take: Kalshi is offering $120,000 to people who play Grand Theft Auto VI and correctly predict the game's commercial performance on their prediction market platform. This matters because it highlights how gaming culture is now bleeding into official workplace engagement strategies, forcing digital workplace leaders to reckon with the blurred lines between work time, personal time, and branded entertainment. Honestly, we've gone from "don't play games at work" to "here's $120k to play games as work," which is either genius or the sign that we've completely given up on office productivity. I'm not entirely sure which.

digital-culture.title: CEOs still think they can get away with affairs after #MeToo
digital-culture.excerpt: Nearly a decade after the #MeToo movement burst into public consciousness, the upheaval at Nvidia may be a lesson in how little CEOs seem to have learned. Nvidia’s embattled CEO, Jensen Huang, has res
digital-culture.dwp_take: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO after the New York Times reported he'd been involved in an affair with a subordinate. This matters because workplace culture flows from leadership, and when executives ignore basic ethical guardrails around power dynamics, it signals that rules don't apply to the top. Nearly a decade into #MeToo and we're apparently still waiting for some leaders to grasp that "don't sleep with people who report to you" isn't a complex moral philosophy.

digital-culture.title: Can we please stop calling it a ‘honey trap’?
digital-culture.excerpt: When Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees on November 8 that he had been “unfaithful” to his wife, there’s a phrase that quickly became omnipresent in the media: Huang had been the victim of a “honey tr
digital-culture.dwp_take: Jensen Huang denied he was ensnared by a "honey trap" after U.S. intelligence suggested a Singapore tech executive had targeted him as part of Chinese espionage efforts. For workplace communicators, this matters because the gendered language we use in crisis scenarios shapes how employees perceive security threats and organizational response. Calling it a honey trap makes it sound like Huang got seduced into stupidity when the real story is likely about sophisticated social engineering, which frankly could happen to anyone paying attention to their job instead of geopolitical counterintelligence.

digital-culture.title: Burnout is a workplace safety hazard. It’s time to start treating it like one
digital-culture.excerpt: Burnout is a huge workplace issue: the low engagement that comes with it costs every business affected a fortune. Worse yet, its effects on workers are deleterious to the point where it can literally
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company ran a piece arguing that burnout should be treated as a genuine workplace safety hazard rather than just an HR problem to solve with yoga apps and meditation subscriptions. This matters because digital workplace leaders are often the ones building the systems and communication channels that either prevent burnout or accelerate it, so you can't outsource this to wellness programs and call it done. Here's the truth: if your collaboration tools are keeping people tethered 24/7 and your culture expects immediate responses at midnight, no amount of free gym memberships will fix what your workplace is actually doing to people.

industry-news.title: This $80 Subscription Will Bring AI Into Your Business
industry-news.excerpt: Tap into the power of OpenAI, Meta, Midjourney, and additional powerful AI models with 1min.AI. The post This $80 Subscription Will Bring AI Into Your Business appeared first on TechRepublic.
industry-news.dwp_take: Some startup is selling access to multiple AI models bundled together for 80 bucks a month. This matters because your users are already cobbling together their own AI toolstack anyway, so a unified interface could actually save money and reduce security headaches. Here's the thing though: if you're still trying to figure out what AI is actually for in your organization, throwing another subscription at the problem is just going to give you an expensive paperweight.

industry-news.title: REDMAGIC 12 Pro vs Galaxy S26 Ultra: Bigger Battery, Surprising Test Results
industry-news.excerpt: REDMAGIC 12 Pro beats Galaxy S26 Ultra in battery endurance tests, but Samsung offers faster charging, better zoom options, and longer software support. The post REDMAGIC 12 Pro vs Galaxy S26 Ultra: B
industry-news.dwp_take: The REDMAGIC 12 Pro outlasted the Galaxy S26 Ultra in battery tests while Samsung countered with faster charging, superior zoom, and longer software support. For digital workplace folks, this matters because your mobile device is basically your office now, and battery life directly impacts productivity and how often you're tethered to a charger. Here's the thing though: in the real world, most of us will never come close to draining either phone before day's end, so pick the one with the features you actually use and call it a win.

industry-news.title: OnePlus’ November Update Adds Automatic Remote PC Unlocking — Here’s Who Gets It
industry-news.excerpt: OnePlus' November update adds automatic remote PC unlocking. Here's how it works, which phones qualify, and why availability differs by region. The post OnePlus’ November Update Adds Automatic Remote
industry-news.dwp_take: OnePlus rolled out a November update that lets certain phones automatically unlock PCs remotely, with availability varying by region and device model. This matters because seamless device authentication across your ecosystem cuts friction from everyday work and reduces password fatigue, which security teams have been nagging us about for years. It's a nice feature, though I'd bet money the regional rollout is more about carrier agreements and regulatory headaches than actual technical limitations, which is peak mobile industry stuff.

industry-news.title: Starlink Mini 2: $999 Preorder Bundle, Specs, and Availability Explained
industry-news.excerpt: Starlink Mini 2 introduces a removable battery offering up to 4.5 hours of connectivity. Here's what buyers should know about the $999 preorder bundle, specifications, and availability. The post Starl
industry-news.dwp_take: Starlink just launched the Mini 2, a portable satellite internet option with a removable battery good for 4.5 hours, priced at $999 for the preorder bundle. For remote workers and hybrid teams, this matters because truly untethered connectivity means your workforce isn't chained to coffee shops or hotel WiFi anymore. That said, $999 is still steep for most employees, and if your company's relying on satellite as a backup plan, you've got bigger infrastructure problems than a fancy gadget can solve.
